title: Non-overlapping Intervals
statement: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap. Touching endpoints do not count as overlap.
hints: Sorting by end time makes the greedy choice obvious: keep the interval that frees the timeline soonest.
If the next interval starts before the last kept end, it overlaps and must be removed.
Otherwise keep it and move the end forward.

approaches.name: Sort by start and dynamic programming
approaches.explanation: Longest non-overlapping subset, then removals are n minus that length.

approaches.name: Greedy by earliest end
approaches.explanation: One pass after sorting by end.

editorial: The minimum deletions equal n minus the size of the largest compatible subset. Activity selection proves that sorting by finish time and taking every interval that starts at or after the last finish is optimal. Count the intervals you skip. Endpoints that merely touch are compatible, so the comparison is strict: start < last_end means overlap.
